gen-gf-oxanium-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC reads dignified, its strokes only gently modulated. Oxanium earns its place big and short, where its round letters look bent from wire and its lowercase stands tall.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-montagu-slab: Oxanium draws every stroke like glowing neon tubing, one thickness from start to finish. Montagu Slab brings a soft, understated shift between heavy downstrokes and slender turns, and that gap is the pair's real charm.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Noto Serif Hentaigana carries a mild, pen-like variation in weight. Against Oxanium, which has no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, that softness becomes the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-ovo: Oxanium's round letters have no tilted stress at all, so they look almost machined, curve after curve. Ovo's moderate stem-to-hairline ratio gives a quiet counterweight.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-bespoke-slab: Loud, loose, and a bit scattered. Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, while Bespoke Slab stands grounded beneath it with tall bodies in every letter, and that grounding is what holds them together.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-erode: Erode reads editorial, with a gentle ebb and flow in its stroke weight. Paprika's hollow-reed counters can take a larger size, but you can leave Erode at a modest size and let its tall middle band do the work.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-trench-slab: Dignified is the word for Trench Slab, whose lowercase sits almost level with its capitals in height, giving it a tidy, upright manner. Paprika is the one that shouts.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-domine: Domine reads refined, with compact ascenders over tall lowercase and a slight pinch where curves meet stems. Over a full page, Domine feels steady and unhurried, while Paprika's loose, scattered letters stay up top making noise.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-esteban: Esteban has a lowercase that looks oversized beside its own capitals, with thin parts barely slimmer than its stems. Paprika is best at loud, spread-out display; Esteban is best at quiet text.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-faustina: Paprika's letters are scattered at a distance, as if they refuse to huddle. Faustina follows with a faintly modulated line and an open-jawed c, so a long stretch of text moves along comfortably and without fuss.
